title: Numbers Become Pictures
tagline: A child's rhyme, a trick with knuckles, and two simple systems that turn the digits 0 to 9 into things you can see.
card: Why numbers are hard to remember, and two beginner systems (shapes and rhymes) that give every digit a picture.
goal: you will learn why numbers are hard to remember, use a shape system and a rhyme system to give every digit a picture, and encode short numbers as one vivid scene.

left_off.q: What is the difference between a palace and a story chain?
left_off.a: A palace uses fixed places for order; a chain uses links between items. A palace is better for long lists, a chain for short quick ones.

left_off.q: Why should you never link item 1 straight to item 5 in a chain?
left_off.a: Each link should hold only two pictures. Each item leads to the next, so the chain stays simple.

left_off.q: What did Parry and Lord find about epic singers?
left_off.a: They remembered the shape of the story and its familiar scenes, and rebuilt the words each time.

text: It is a wet afternoon and a child is trying to remember how many days there are in each month. Her grandmother does not give her a table. She says a rhyme that her own grandmother said, and that has been said in English for hundreds of years:
Thirty days hath September, April, June and November. All the rest have thirty-one, except for February alone.
The child says it three times, and by the end of the afternoon she has twelve numbers in her head that she will keep for the rest of her life.

check.q: How does the rhyme help the child?
check.a: The rhythm and the rhyme carry the numbers, so she remembers the sound of the verse, and the verse brings back the numbers.

parts.talk: Do you know any rhyme or song that helps you remember a fact? Say it.

text: Then the grandmother shows her another trick. She makes a fist and says: 'Count the knuckles and the dips between them.' Every knuckle is a long month with thirty-one days; every dip is a short month. January is the first knuckle, February the first dip, March the next knuckle. When she gets to the last knuckle, July, she jumps back to the first one for August, and the pattern carries on.
The child can now check any month in a few seconds, anywhere, with no rhyme and no paper. The numbers have been put in a place you can see and touch.

check.q: How does the knuckle trick work?
check.a: Knuckles are the thirty-one-day months and dips are the shorter months; you count along the hand.

parts.talk: Which would you use, the rhyme or the knuckles? Why?

text: A rhyme and a hand can hold twelve numbers. But what about a phone number, a PIN, a year, a passport number, a bank code? Numbers like these are hard for a simple reason: a number is not a picture. The digits 7, 3, 9 do not look like anything and mean nothing. The mind has nothing to hold on to, and it lets go.

The answer is the oldest trick in this course: give them pictures. In this room you will meet two simple systems for doing it. One gives each digit a picture by its shape; the other gives each digit a picture by a rhyme. In the next room you will learn a stronger system, but these two are quick to learn and are a good start.

check.q: Why are numbers so hard to remember?
check.a: A number is not a picture. The digits mean nothing by themselves, so there is nothing for the mind to hold on to.

parts.talk: Which numbers in your life do you remember? Why do you think you remember those?

method.x: Both systems have the same limit: one picture per digit. A twelve-digit number needs twelve pictures. For long numbers you will want something that packs more in, and that is the Major System, next.

try.title: Shape or rhyme?
try.prompt: Match each digit to its picture in the shape system.

try.title: Rhyme
try.prompt: Match each digit to its picture in the rhyme system.

try.title: Encode 25 (shape)
try.prompt: Shape system: 2 is a swan and 5 is a hook. Make one vivid scene for the number 25.
try.model: A huge black swan has a rusty hook caught on its neck and is dragging a fisherman across the lake, roaring like a motor-boat.
checks: The swan comes before the hook.

try.title: Encode 67 and 84 (shape)
try.prompt: 6 is a cherry, 7 a cliff, 8 a snowman, 4 a sailboat. Make a scene for 67 and another for 84.
try.model: 67: A cherry the size of a car rolls off the edge of a cliff, bouncing and splashing. 84: A snowman is sailing a little sailboat across a sea of hot chocolate, melting as he goes.
checks: Each scene is vivid and moving.
They do not blur into each other.

try.title: Encode 39 and 51 (rhyme)
try.prompt: Rhyme system: 3 tree, 9 vine; 5 hive, 1 bun. Make one scene for 39 and one for 51.
try.model: 39: A tree with a vine wrapped around its trunk, which is pulling it over like a rope. 51: A beehive in the middle of a hot bun, and the bees are eating the crumbs.
checks: Each scene is vivid and moving.

try.title: A four-digit number
try.prompt: Use either system to encode 1776. Split it into 17 and 76 and make two scenes. Write them.
try.model: Shape: 17 = candle + cliff: a candle burns on top of a high cliff and gives off blue smoke. 76 = cliff + cherry: another cliff throws a huge cherry into the sea. Two scenes, four digits.
checks: I split the number into two pairs.
Each scene has two pictures acting on each other.

try.title: Tell the scenes
try.prompt: Say the scene for 42, 73, 25 and 67 aloud, then say the numbers back.

quiz.q: Why is a number hard to remember?
quiz.why: A number has no picture, so there is nothing to hold on to.

quiz.q: What is the limit of the shape and rhyme systems?
opts: They cannot be used for years
One picture per digit, so long numbers become very long
They only work for odd numbers
quiz.why: Each digit needs its own picture, so long numbers need many.

quiz.q: In the rhyme system, what is 8?
In the shape system, what is 4?

challenge.title: Memory challenge: five famous years
challenge.intro: Encode these five years, in this order, using whichever system you prefer: 1066 (Battle of Hastings), 1215 (Magna Carta), 1492 (Columbus sails), 1776 (US independence), 1989 (Berlin Wall falls). Put each year in one scene.
challenge.study: Split each year into pairs and make a scene. One scene per year, in order.

look_back.q: What is a link, and what is a chain?
look_back.a: A link is a picture of two items acting on each other; a chain is a row of links.
One place along the palace route where you put a picture.

look_back.q: Name three tools for making a picture stick.
look_back.a: For example: movement, exaggeration, colour, humour, a number.
